chunks: And a group narrated to me, from Harun ibn Musa, from Muhammad ibn Himam, who said:

Abdullah ibn Ja'far al-Himyari said: When Abu Amr passed away, letters continued to arrive with the same handwriting through which we used to receive news of the establishment of Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) in his place.

key_terms.أبو جعفر: Abu Ja'far, the second special emissary, son of the Imam
key_terms.أبو عمرو: Abu Amr, the first of the four special emissaries of the Imam
key_terms.إقامة: Establishment or appointment in a position
key_terms.الخط: The handwriting, used as a sign of authenticity for the Imam's letters
key_terms.مقامه: His place/position, referring to the role of the emissary

ai.seo_question: How did the Shia community verify the Imam's succession during the Minor Occultation?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Kitab al-Ghayba* underscores the continuity of divine authority during the Minor Occultation (*al-Ghayb al-Sughra*) by highlighting the identical handwriting of the Imam in letters from both the first and second emissaries. It serves as a crucial *hujjah* (proof) for the Shia community, validating the legitimacy of the successive *Nuwwab al-Arba’ah* (Four Deputies) and ensuring the unbroken chain of religious guidance despite the Imam's physical absence.
